assessment: In this timely study, Nagappan and Franks challenge a long-held model of sequential odor processing by two classes of excitatory principal neurons in the olfactory cortex (semilunar neurons and superficial pyramidal neurons). The main findings of this study support an alternate interpretation that semilunar and pyramidal neurons process olfactory information in parallel rather than sequentially. This work is highly relevant to the olfactory field as well as those scientists who aim to understand the roles of diverse neural classes in sensory processing. The work is executed very well, properly controlled and analysed, and the claims are very well supported by the data.
